title.narrative: UNICEF, with the government and young people, has driven evidence-based, participatory initiatives for adolescent development and participation. Key achievements include launching the first National Youth Mental Health Index, rolling out the Helping Adolescents Thrive (HAT) tools, and developing a robust monitoring and evaluation framework for mental health with the government and WHO. UNICEF capacitated youth advocacy champions who engaged 1,527 young people on their rights, supported adolescents in informing the Children?s Commissioner?s reform agenda, and supported CSOs with amplifying 321 children's voices in the CRC Children?s report. Young people's participation has been integral to informing UNICEF?s new Country Programme Document.
